headline: Generosity is giving freely—sharing resources, time, and care with others
universal_truth: What you give expands you; generosity flows outward and returns transformed
fun_facts: Generous people report higher happiness than those who spend only on themselves
Generosity activates reward centers in the brain—giving literally feels good
Small regular acts of generosity have more impact than occasional large ones
discussion_questions: What do you give—time, money, attention, skills?
When is generosity wise and when might it deplete you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You have something others need. Time, skills, money, attention, care—resources flow through you. Generosity is the choice to let some flow outward. Sharing what you have connects you to others.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Why give away what you could keep? Isn't self-interest more rational?

options.text: Generosity benefits the giver too—it creates connection, meaning, and happiness that keeping can't provide; what you give becomes relationship; what you hoard stays just stuff
options.response: Yes. Generosity isn't just altruism—it's wise living. Giving builds bonds, creates meaning, activates happiness. The generous life is richer than the hoarding life, even with less stuff.
True of material things, but generosity often generates returns—relationships, opportunities, meaning...

q1.title: Many Forms
q1.script: Generosity isn't just money. Time, attention, skills, care—these are gifts. Sometimes presence matters more than presents. Give what you have, not just what you can buy.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Many Forms"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Sustainable Giving
q2.script: Depleting yourself isn't generosity—it's martyrdom. Sustainable giving comes from overflow, not depletion. Fill your own cup enough to share without emptying.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Without Strings
q3.script: True generosity gives without expectation of return. Gifts with strings attached are transactions. Give freely, and if something returns, receive it as bonus rather than payment.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What you give expands you. Generosity flows outward and returns transformed. Share what you have.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 343. Tomorrow, we'll explore accepting what's given—receiving. Until then, consider what you have to give.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Generosity Practice - What Can You Give?
growTrack.activity: What resources do you have—time, skills, money, attention? What could you give today? Practice one act of generosity: help someone, share something, give your full attention. Notice how it feels.
